annotations.text:
Volume belongs to the task, not the phone.
Every alarm keeps its own level, as a share of the Ringer & Alerts volume iOS rings alarms at: 100% is that volume, 50% half of it. No app can play a sound the way the Lock Screen alarm will, so there is no live preview — Test real alarm rings the real thing 5 s later, at the tone and level on screen, and what you hear is what wakes you. Swipe left on a row to delete.

Editing an alarm.
New alarms open on the current time, carrying the volume, sound, snooze and vibration of the last alarm saved. Saving switches an alarm on. The slider is silent; Test real alarm rings the real alarm 5 s later with what is on screen, and while it is on its way the button reads Cancel test with a countdown (not drawn here). The caption says the Ringer & Alerts volume sets the maximum, and where to change it. Vibrate buzzes while the alarm rings in the app; on the Lock Screen, iOS's Haptics setting decides. With AlarmKit allowed (iOS 26) every alarm rings through Silent, so the Override Silent switch is not shown.

Picking a sound.
Tapping a tone picks it and plays a short preview as media, at the phone's media volume, just to recognise it; the button rings the real alarm 5 s later with that tone at the alarm's level. iOS does not share its own tone library with apps, so the choices are the bundled tones and your own audio from Music or Files. iOS caps alarm sounds at 30 s: a longer song rings from its start and stops at 29 s — the import says so at once, and the tone's row keeps saying it.

Ringing in the app.
A small Snooze, and Stop as a slide so a stray tap cannot silence the alarm. On the Lock Screen, iOS draws the ringing alarm itself; apps only set its button text, icon and colour.

Snoozed, on the Lock Screen.
The dark card is the app's Live Activity counting down to when the alarm returns; it keeps the same colours in both themes. The notice below it is posted the moment you snooze, so a snooze is never invisible.

Sounds and Settings.
Sounds plays a tone as media when you tap it, and rings the real alarm 5 s later at the chosen tone and level — the only honest audition. Settings holds membership, what happens when an alarm rings, the clock, the theme, and the language — English or ไทย, each named in itself. The language choice only appears on a phone that lists Thai among its languages; anywhere else the app is English. Membership, at the top: the free plan keeps up to 3 alarms and members have no limit; at the limit the + button explains and offers membership, and every alarm already set keeps ringing. The price comes from the App Store; a sideloaded build can show the plan but not sell it. New-alarm defaults are learned from saved alarms rather than set here.

Light
When the phone is in light mode. Appearance is Auto on first launch, so the app follows the phone — as does the clock, which starts on Match device. Warm paper neutrals; amber deepens for text and icons so it holds contrast on white.

Dark
When the phone is in dark mode. Same layout; either theme can be pinned in Settings › Appearance.

Thai
The same screens with the app in ไทย. First launch picks Thai when the phone is set to Thai, and English for any other language; Settings › Language switches at once. Labels, days, tone names, notifications and the Lock Screen countdown all read Thai; task names are the user's own.

Thai, dark
The same, in dark mode.
